record_identity.title: Authenticity Debt research preprint issued incorrect provenance references and later corrections

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Authenticity Debt arXiv preprint of 30 May 2026 and corrected revision of 2 November 2026
incident_identity.date_basis: The artefact was first public on 2026-05-30; 4 November 2026 is the date of external discovery and scrutiny, not a claim of continuous writing or publication up to that day. For revised papers each later version is part of the same publication occurrence.

summary: On 30 May 2026, Accenture-affiliated researchers posted Authenticity Debt, a research preprint about synthetic-content provenance and trustworthy AI governance, on arXiv. Its original reference list included bibliographic discrepancies: reference 5 described a paper under a title that did not match arXiv:2509.13365, and reference 15 linked to a purported FraudGPT GitHub repository rather than an attributable research publication. The authors posted a revised version on 2 November, correcting the paper title and replacing the FraudGPT reference with a named Netenrich article. On 4 November GPTZero reported nine seriously distorted citations among 54 original references and alleged that the earlier GitHub link led to malware; the malware claim has not been independently verified. The source errors and later revision are observable, but the specific role of generative AI in the writing or citation assembly is unconfirmed.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The arXiv v1 bibliography supplied an incorrect title with identifier 2509.13365, as directly compared with the actual arXiv record. Its reference 15 pointed to a purported FraudGPT repository; the public investigation asserts malware at that link, but no independent security analysis or infection record is reviewed here. ArXiv's v2 dated 2 November replaces reference 5 with the real title The Provenance Problem: LLMs and the Breakdown of Citation Norms and reference 15 with the Netenrich writeup. GPTZero 4 November reports nine significantly incorrect citations among 54 in the originally audited publication, and explicitly states an AI-detector score does not prove model use. The date of corrections predates that external investigation, so no causal claim that GPTZero forced the corrections is warranted.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The assessed conduct is the release and research-stage reliance on specific unfaithful citations and claims within Authenticity Debt. The suspected participating generative-AI research/drafting component has not been identified; public output and independently checkable source discrepancies nevertheless show material below the epistemic assurance appropriate for publication. The cause remains disputed or unverified: the resulting provisional Epistemic Reliance Calibration failure applies to the observable generated/retrieved/transformed/synthesised epistemic artefact as it was supplied for scholarly or policy reliance, not an assertion that any identified LLM generated the error. The authors and publishing bodies are accountable for publication, but the available evidence does not assign the erroneous words to a specific person, model or tool. External GPTZero detection is not the assessed AI platform.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This occurrence illustrates the separation between observable deficient epistemic assurance and unknown internal generative-system topology. Professional reliance requires source verification proportionate to publication-stage evidentiary use even where model trace and authorship details are unavailable. The correction or investigator response can be recorded without transferring its actions to the assessed synthetic component.
assessment_boundaries: The preprint is by researchers affiliated with Accenture and is not represented as a formally published Accenture corporate report.
The original title/identifier mismatch and replacement are verifiable against dated arXiv versions; nine-of-54 is GPTZero's attributed tally, not a fresh independent recount.
The assertion that a now-deleted repository contained live malware is made by GPTZero and was not independently forensically verified here. No reader infection or harm is established.
The revision was submitted on 2 November 2026, before the 4 November public investigation. Its timing does not establish notice, reason or whether every disputed reference was fixed.
A real arXiv article was misidentified; the later version repaired some title/source descriptions. No unreported original author workflow, model or prompt is inferred.
The research paper's content about authenticity and provenance is not independently disproved by the existence of incorrect citations.
The original publication and its revision are one occurrence; the version 2 corrections are not a separate platform or AI system to classify.
Any FC-062 result is expressly provisional pending further source evidence of generative AI participation, not a legal or scholarly finding of deliberate deception.
Publication/author workflow uncertainty is reported as a limitation, not falsely resolved through hypothetical prompts or model selection.
No independently acting defender AI is assessed in this incident; post-publication investigations and corrections are source/outcome context.
